Model the vintage robbie the banker coin bank toy using the reference image

Reference files (read them, don't modify them), in ./references/:
- ./references/robie.jpg

Make it in Blender, working in the current directory.
- A Blender 5 instance is running for you with no window (background mode). Use it through the `blender`
  MCP tools: run Python (`bpy`) with execute_blender_code, and look things up with the API and manual
  search tools. Blender's working directory is the current directory. The scene starts as Blender's
  default one (a cube, a camera and a light).
- There is no window to screenshot. To check your work, render it to an image file and look at the image
  (render_thumbnail_to_path, render_viewport_to_path, or a render of the scene camera to a file).
  Keep renders quick: a single tool call may take at most 5 minutes.
- Build it in Blender itself; don't write the model or the images any other way.
- Save the finished result in ./output/ (only what is in ./output/ is published):
  - the model or scene as one .glb file (glTF binary), shown on the site in an interactive 3D viewer:
    `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=..., export_format='GLB')`, without Draco or meshopt
    compression, at most 15 MB;
  - one or more final renders as .png or .jpg, at most 2 MB each, from camera angles you choose.
  At most 8 files in all.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.12.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything (no asset
  libraries or add-ons).
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

Read image file `./references/robie.jpg` as model-visible image output.

import bpy, math
from mathutils import Vector

# Clear scene
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
for coll in list(bpy.data.collections):
    if coll.name != "Collection":
        pass
# clean meshes/curves
for block in [bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.curves, bpy.data.cameras, bpy.data.lights]:
    pass

scene = bpy.context.scene
scene.render.engine = 'BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT' if 'BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT' in [e.identifier for e in bpy.types.RenderEngine.__subclasses__()] else 'BLENDER_EEVEE'
# Actually set eevee
try:
    scene.render.engine = 'BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT'
except:
    scene.render.engine = 'BLENDER_EEVEE'

# Materials
def make_mat(name, color, roughness=0.35, metallic=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m: bpy.data.materials.remove(m)
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = roughness
    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = metallic
    return m

yellow = make_mat("YellowPlastic", (1.0, 0.78, 0.02), 0.22)
yellow2 = make_mat("YellowPlastic2", (1.0, 0.82, 0.08), 0.25)
black = make_mat("BlackPlastic", (0.015,0.015,0.015), 0.35)
black_gloss = make_mat("BlackGloss", (0.01,0.01,0.01), 0.18)
dark_grey = make_mat("DarkGrey", (0.08,0.08,0.08), 0.4)
white = make_mat("White", (1,1,1), 0.3)
eye_white = make_mat("EyeWhite", (0.96,0.94,0.88), 0.15)
brown = make_mat("EyeRim", (0.28,0.18,0.08), 0.35)
pupil_mat = make_mat("Pupil", (0.0,0.0,0.0), 0.15)

def assign(obj, mat):
    if obj.data and hasattr(obj.data, "materials"):
        obj.data.materials.append(mat)

def smooth(obj):
    if obj.type=='MESH':
        for p in obj.data.polygons:
            p.use_smooth = True

# Helpers
def cone(name, loc, r1, r2, depth, mat, verts=48):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(vertices=verts, radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=loc)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; assign(o,mat); smooth(o); return o

def cyl(name, loc, radius, depth, mat, verts=48, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=verts, radius=radius, depth=depth, location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; assign(o,mat); smooth(o); return o

def sphere(name, loc, scale, mat, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(radius=1, location=loc, rotation=rot, segments=32, ring_count=24)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; o.scale=scale; assign(o,mat); smooth(o); return o

def cube(name, loc, scale, mat, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; o.scale=scale; assign(o,mat); return o

def torus(name, loc, major, minor, mat, rot=(0,0,0)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=major, minor_radius=minor, major_segments=48, minor_segments=12, location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name; assign(o,mat); smooth(o); return o

# === BASE & BODY ===
# black base disc
cyl("BaseBlack", (0,0,0.06), 0.98, 0.12, black_gloss)
# thin black bottom rim slightly larger
cyl("BaseRim", (0,0,0.13), 0.97, 0.05, black)

# lower body - bell shape: bottom wide, top narrower
body = cone("Body", (0,0,0.68), 0.96, 0.84, 1.05, yellow)
# add subtle bevel via modifier
mod = body.modifiers.new("bev","BEVEL"); mod.width=0.025; mod.segments=2

# vertical seam line on front of body - very thin dark line box
seam = cube("BodySeam", (0,-0.885,0.68), (0.006,0.01,0.48), dark_grey)
seam.scale = (0.006,0.008,0.48)

# head separator black line
cyl("HeadGap", (0,0,1.235), 0.86, 0.035, black)

# HEAD
head = cone("Head", (0,0,1.66), 0.88, 0.86, 0.82, yellow)
mod = head.modifiers.new("bev","BEVEL"); mod.width=0.03; mod.segments=2

# head top black disc - slightly inset oval top
top = cyl("HeadTopBlack", (0,0,2.08), 0.80, 0.045, black_gloss)
top.scale = (1,1,1)
# thin ribbed lines on top - 5 thin boxes on top back area
for i in range(5):
    y = 0.28 + i*0.07
    b = cube(f"TopRib_{i}", (0, y, 2.105), (0.55 - i*0.04, 0.012, 0.004), dark_grey)

# === EYES ===
# Front is -Y. Eyes on front face of head
for sx, label in [(-0.34,"L"), (0.34,"R")]:
    # socket rim - torus facing forward (rotate X 90deg)
    t = torus(f"EyeRim_{label}", (sx, -0.86, 1.78), 0.185, 0.028, brown, rot=(math.radians(90),0,0))
    # dark socket disc
    c = cyl(f"EyeSocket_{label}", (sx, -0.855, 1.78), 0.185, 0.03, black, rot=(math.radians(90),0,0))
    # eyeball white sphere protruding
    e = sphere(f"Eyeball_{label}", (sx, -0.89, 1.78), (0.16,0.10,0.16), eye_white)
    # pupil - black flattened sphere low on eyeball (looking down)
    p = sphere(f"Pupil_{label}", (sx, -0.975, 1.70), (0.095,0.04,0.075), pupil_mat)

# small white teeth under head gap centre front
for sx in [-0.07, 0.07]:
    tth = cube(f"Tooth_{sx}", (sx, -0.845, 1.20), (0.045,0.02,0.055), white)
    # round a bit via bevel
    m = tth.modifiers.new("b","BEVEL"); m.width=0.015; m.segments=2

# coin slot on back of head (+Y side)
slot = cube("CoinSlotBack", (0, 0.865, 1.38), (0.09,0.015,0.018), black)

# === SHOULDERS ===
for sx, label in [(-1, "L"), (1,"R")]:
    # shoulder cap cylinder axis X
    s = cyl(f"Shoulder_{label}", (sx*0.88, 0, 1.02), 0.20, 0.18, yellow, rot=(0, math.radians(90),0))
    # inner dark ring
    s2 = cyl(f"ShoulderRing_{label}", (sx*0.96, 0, 1.02), 0.13, 0.04, black, rot=(0, math.radians(90),0))

# === ARMS (curves) ===
def tube_arm(name, points, radius=0.075):
    cu = bpy.data.curves.new(name, type='CURVE')
    cu.dimensions='3D'
    cu.resolution_u=2
    cu.bevel_depth=radius
    cu.bevel_resolution=3
    cu.fill_mode='FULL'
    sp = cu.splines.new('BEZIER')
    sp.bezier_points.add(len(points)-1)
    for i, co in enumerate(points):
        bp = sp.bezier_points[i]
        bp.co = co
        bp.handle_left_type='AUTO'
        bp.handle_right_type='AUTO'
    ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, cu)
    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob)
    ob.data.materials.append(black)
    return ob

# Tray arm: on -X side (viewer right in front view when camera at -Y? we place tray on -X)
# shoulder at (-0.95,0,1.02) -> out -> forward -> in to tray
tube_arm("Arm_Tray", [(-0.96,0,1.02), (-1.18,-0.05,0.92), (-1.22,-0.35,0.78), (-1.08,-0.68,0.76), (-0.78,-0.82,0.78)], 0.07)
# Hook arm: on +X side, hangs down and curls into C
tube_arm("Arm_Hook", [(0.96,0,1.02), (1.18,-0.02,0.90), (1.24,-0.08,0.62), (1.18,-0.18,0.38), (1.02,-0.22,0.32), (0.92,-0.18,0.44), (0.96,-0.12,0.54)], 0.07)

# small cuff rings at arm ends
torus("ArmCuff_Tray", (-1.08,-0.68,0.76), 0.085, 0.02, black_gloss, rot=(0.6,0.4,0))
torus("ArmCuff_Hook", (1.24,-0.08,0.62), 0.085, 0.02, black_gloss, rot=(0,0,0))

# === COIN TRAY ===
# flat black disc held forward on tray arm end
tray = cyl("CoinTray", (-0.58,-0.92,0.80), 0.30, 0.035, black_gloss, rot=(0,0,0))
# tray has a small tab pointing outward
tab = cube("TrayTab", (-0.32,-0.78,0.80), (0.10,0.07,0.018), black_gloss, rot=(0,0,math.radians(-30)))
m=tab.modifiers.new("b","BEVEL"); m.width=0.02; m.segments=2
# white ring on tray
ring = torus("TrayRing", (-0.58,-0.92,0.822), 0.19, 0.012, white, rot=(0,0,0))
# $ will be text later

# === FEET ===
for sx, label in [(-1,"L"), (1,"R")]:
    # black sole
    sole = sphere(f"FootSole_{label}", (sx*0.78, -0.48, 0.10), (0.26,0.58,0.09), black_gloss)
    sole.rotation_euler = (0,0, math.radians(sx*-12))
    # yellow foot - elongated teardrop: sphere scaled, pointed front
    foot = sphere(f"Foot_{label}", (sx*0.78, -0.48, 0.17), (0.24,0.55,0.16), yellow)
    foot.rotation_euler = (0,0, math.radians(sx*-12))
    # groove lines on foot - two thin dark tori sliced? use thin boxes curved - approximate with thin boxes across foot
    for gi in range(2):
        yoff = 0.08 + gi*0.09
        g = cube(f"FootGroove_{label}_{gi}", (sx*0.78 - sx*0.02, -0.48 + yoff -0.18, 0.315), (0.20,0.012,0.008), dark_grey, rot=(0,0, math.radians(sx*-12)))

# === TEXT: ROBIE on chest ===
def add_text(name, text, loc, size, mat, rot=(math.radians(90),0,0), extrude=0.008):
    bpy.ops.object.text_add(location=loc, rotation=rot)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name
    o.data.body=text
    o.data.size=size
    o.data.align_x='CENTER'
    o.data.align_y='CENTER'
    o.data.extrude=extrude
    o.data.materials.append(mat)
    # make bold-ish by shear? keep
    return o

# ROBIE - front chest, facing -Y: text rotation: need facing -Y. Text default in XY plane facing +Z. Rotate X -90 makes it face -Y? Let's rotate X 90deg? We'll set rot X = 90deg (?) test: rotation (90,0,180) often for front facing -Y
robie = add_text("Text_ROBIE", "ROBIE", (-0.28, -0.905, 1.02), 0.17, black, rot=(math.radians(90),0,math.radians(180)))
robie.data.space_character=1.05

# $ on tray - horizontal on top of tray facing up
dollar = add_text("Text_Dollar", "$", (-0.58,-0.92,0.825), 0.28, white, rot=(0,0,math.radians(180)))

# Radio Shack text on top (small, white) - horizontal
rs = add_text("Text_TopBrand", "Radio Shack", (0, -0.18, 2.105), 0.11, white, rot=(0,0,math.radians(180)))
rs2 = add_text("Text_TopSub", "ROBOTIC BANKER", (0, -0.02, 2.105), 0.055, white, rot=(0,0,math.radians(180)))

result={"ok": True, "objects": [o.name for o in bpy.context.scene.objects]}

Finished — the vintage Robie the Robotic Banker coin bank is modeled in Blender and published in `./output/`.

What I made:
- Glossy lemon-yellow two-tier cylindrical body and head with black separator line, thin black base rim, tiny white teeth under the head gap, a back coin slot, and a black ribbed top disc lettered “Radio Shack / ROBOTIC BANKER.”
- Recessed cup eyes with brown rims, white eyeballs, and large pupils looking down, plus bold “ROBIE” lettering on the chest.
- Yellow shoulder discs with two distinct black arms — a compact C-hook on the left and a forward arm on the right holding the black coin tray with a white ring and “$” emblem — and splayed yellow feet with black soles.
